intro: Excerpts copied from the live Claude Voice source (C:\CLAUDE\Claude Voice). Each shows the real code behind a capability and explains how it powers that feature. Nothing about which AI answers, which voice is used, or which channel is on is hardcoded — it all lives in config.json + secrets/claude_voice.env.

sections.category: Claude-CLI Bridge — the free real Claude

snippets.title: Drive headless `claude -p` on the subscription token
snippets.feature: Real Claude, for free (claude_cli backend)
snippets.code:
claude = cfg.get("bin") or shutil.which("claude")
if not claude:
    raise RuntimeError("claude CLI not found on PATH")
system = "\n".join(m["content"] for m in messages if m.get("role") == "system")
convo = []
for m in messages:
    if m.get("role") == "system":
        continue
    who = "the owner" if m.get("role") == "user" else "Claude"
    convo.append(f"{who}: {m['content']}")
prompt = "\n".join(convo) if convo else "(no message)"
args = [claude, "-p", "--output-format", "text",
        "--no-session-persistence", "--model", cfg.get("model", "sonnet")]
if system:
    args += ["--append-system-prompt", system]
# NOT --bare, because --bare forces ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and would bypass the free subscription token.
proc = subprocess.run(args, input=prompt, capture_output=True, text=True,
                      timeout=cfg.get("timeout", 90), cwd=tempfile.gettempdir())
snippets.explanation:
This is the heart of the project. It spawns the local Claude Code CLI as a subprocess, passing the conversation over STDIN and the system prompt via --append-system-prompt. The cwd is a neutral temp dir so no project CLAUDE.md is auto-loaded each turn (speed). It deliberately avoids --bare because --bare would force the metered ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — instead it relies on the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN subscription token, which is what makes the real Claude FREE here.  

_Note: this excerpt is sanitised — identifiers naming the owner have been replaced with a generic term, per the project rule that no real person's name appears in documentation. The underlying source is unchanged._

snippets.title: Detect a broken/expired login and report honestly
snippets.feature: Self-diagnosing real-Claude path
snippets.code:
blob = (proc.stdout or "") + (proc.stderr or "")
if "Not logged in" in blob or "/login" in blob:
    raise RuntimeError("claude CLI not authenticated for headless use — run `claude setup-token` "
                       "(free, uses your subscription) and set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN")
out = (proc.stdout or "").strip()
if not out:
    raise RuntimeError(f"claude CLI returned nothing (rc={proc.returncode}): {(proc.stderr or '')[:200]}")
yield out
snippets.explanation: Rather than fail silently, the backend inspects the CLI output for the tell-tale 'Not logged in' / '/login' strings and raises a precise, actionable error telling the owner to re-run `claude setup-token`. This is exactly what the hourly health monitor surfaces — a stale subscription token is the single most likely failure of the free real-Claude path, so it gets named explicitly.

snippets.title: Synchronous bridge round-trip (legacy file bus)
snippets.feature: Blocking real-Claude turn for voice loops
snippets.explanation: The original 'bridge' engine: it drops a message into claude_bridge/inbox.jsonl and polls outbox.jsonl for a reply with the matching id, up to a timeout. The catch — proven in production — is that NO program answers; a human had to type the reply (1 of 12 ever answered). This is why the claude_cli backend replaced it; the round-trip remains for back-compat and is slated for deletion (MASTER_PLAN task B1).

snippets.title: Local Whisper, CPU int8
snippets.feature: On-device transcription, free and private
snippets.code:
def load_whisper(cfg):
    from faster_whisper import WhisperModel
    model = cfg["stt"]["model"]
    # CPU only: faster-whisper CUDA needs cublas/cuDNN DLLs absent from this Windows Python.
    m = WhisperModel(model, device="cpu", compute_type="int8")
    log(f"[STT] faster-whisper '{model}' on cpu (int8)")
    return m

def transcribe(model, audio, cfg):
    wav = os.path.join(TMP, "cv_utt.wav")
    sf.write(wav, audio, SR)
    segs, info = model.transcribe(wav, language=cfg["stt"].get("language"), beam_size=5,
                                  initial_prompt=brain.stt_hint(cfg))
    text = " ".join(s.text for s in segs).strip()
    return text, getattr(info, "language", None)
snippets.explanation: Transcription runs entirely on-device with faster-whisper, so speech never leaves the machine and costs nothing. It is pinned to CPU int8 because the CUDA DLLs are missing from this Windows Python (the LiveKit rebuild restores GPU). The initial_prompt is brain.stt_hint() — a bias toward the brain names so 'Claude' isn't misheard as 'Cloud'.

snippets.title: Energy VAD — hands-free endpointing
snippets.feature: Auto start/stop without key presses
snippets.explanation: The built-in voice-activity detector needs no extra dependencies: it computes per-block RMS energy, starts capturing when energy crosses start_rms, and ends the turn after enough trailing silence (silence_ms) once a minimum speech length is met. min_speech_ms and max_utterance_s guard against noise blips and runaway recordings. config.listening.mode chooses vad, wake, or push-to-talk.

snippets.title: Mishearing-tolerant brain-name bias
snippets.feature: Whisper hears 'Claude', not 'Cloud'
snippets.code:
def stt_hint(cfg=None):
    """initial_prompt for faster-whisper that biases it to transcribe the brain names
    CORRECTLY (so 'Claude' doesn't come out as 'Cloud')."""
    names = " and ".join(sorted(display_names(cfg)))
    return f"the owner is talking to his AI assistants {names}."
snippets.explanation:
Whisper frequently hears 'Claude' as 'Cloud'. Passing this sentence as the initial_prompt biases the decoder toward the actual brain names (Claude and Ronald), improving the odds that an address command is transcribed correctly. It is paired with homophone address_terms and a fuzzy fallback in the router for the cases Whisper still gets wrong.  

_Note: this excerpt is sanitised — identifiers naming the owner have been replaced with a generic term, per the project rule that no real person's name appears in documentation. The underlying source is unchanged._

snippets.title: edge-tts neural voice with offline fallback
snippets.feature: Claude speaks (MALE) — robust playback
snippets.code:
DEFAULT_EDGE = "en-US-AndrewNeural"   # Claude's voice is MALE
PT_EDGE = "pt-BR-AntonioNeural"

def speak_edge(text, voice, rate="+0%"):
    import edge_tts
    try:
        import pronounce
        text = pronounce.apply(text)  # spoken-only fixes (e.g. The owner -> Renee)
    except Exception:
        pass
    path = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "claude_say.mp3")
    asyncio.run(edge_tts.Communicate(text, voice, rate=rate).save(path))
    _play(path)
# ... in main(): engine 'auto' -> edge if installed else sapi; on edge failure, fall back to SAPI.
snippets.explanation:
Claude's voice defaults to the warm MALE en-US-AndrewNeural (Antonio for Portuguese). The text is run through pronounce.apply for speech-only fixes, synthesised by Microsoft's free neural edge-tts, and played via ffplay. If edge-tts or the network is unavailable, main() falls back to offline Windows SAPI — so the PC can always talk, online or not.  

_Note: this excerpt is sanitised — identifiers naming the owner have been replaced with a generic term, per the project rule that no real person's name appears in documentation. The underlying source is unchanged._

snippets.title: Per-sentence streaming TTS + barge-in
snippets.feature: Claude starts speaking on the first sentence; can be interrupted
snippets.explanation: Instead of waiting for the whole answer, speak_stream consumes the brain's token stream, flushes each complete sentence (ending in . ! ? ; or newline) to edge-tts, and plays it as it arrives — so Claude begins talking almost immediately. play_interruptible watches the microphone during playback and terminates ffplay if the user starts speaking (barge-in), which is disabled by default to avoid self-trigger without headphones.

snippets.title: Spoken-only pronunciation rewrite
snippets.feature: Say 'Renee', print 'the owner'
snippets.explanation:
Neural TTS would say 'the owner' wrong, so this whole-word, case-preserving substitution rewrites it to 'Renee' (ruh-NAY) in the audio only — the printed text is untouched. The map is merged from a built-in default plus config.json voice.pronunciation, so the owner can add new spoken fixes without touching code.  

_Note: this excerpt is sanitised — identifiers naming the owner have been replaced with a generic term, per the project rule that no real person's name appears in documentation. The underlying source is unchanged._

snippets.title: Address a brain by name (mishearing-tolerant)
snippets.feature: Say 'Claude' to wake the real me
snippets.explanation: Detects when the owner opens by naming a brain. It strips a leading filler word, matches the brain's address_terms (which deliberately include Whisper mishearings like 'cloud'/'claud'/'clawed'), and as a last resort accepts the first token within Levenshtein distance 1 of a name. This is what makes 'Claude, ...' reliably switch to the real Claude even when speech recognition is imperfect.

snippets.title: Resolve a turn: route, switch, or take-a-break
snippets.feature: Name toggle + wake + hand-over, in one place
snippets.code:
if locked or not bcfg.get("address_toggle", True):
    _fill(result, cfg, reg, active)            # hard-set: ignore name toggles
    return result
name, rest = _match_address(text, reg)
if name is None:
    _fill(result, cfg, reg, active); return result   # current brain answers
if rest != "" and _is_break(rest, bcfg):
    other = _other(reg, name); set_active(other, bcfg)
    result["control_reply"] = (f"Okay — {reg[name]['display_name']} stepping back. "
                               f"{reg[other]['display_name']} is taking over now.")
    result["route"] = False; _fill(result, cfg, reg, other); return result
set_active(name, bcfg)                          # addressing a brain makes it active
if rest == "":
    result["control_reply"] = f"{reg[name]['display_name']} here. Go ahead."
    result["route"] = False
snippets.explanation: The single decision point shared by every surface. When locked, name toggles are ignored (a true hard-set). Otherwise: '<name>, take a break' hands to the other brain; a bare name wakes-and-greets with no LLM call; and a real message routes to the addressed brain. route=False marks pure control commands so the channel replies with the spoken confirmation directly.

snippets.title: Ronald's anti-hallucination identity
snippets.feature: The local stand-in never pretends to be Claude
snippets.code:
"ronald": {
  "display_name": "Ronald",
  "engine": "ollama",
  "address_terms": ["ronald", "ronaldo", "ronnie", "ronold", "donald"],
  "voice": "en-US-BrianNeural",
  "system_prompt": "You are Ronald, the owner's LOCAL stand-in assistant running on his own PC (a small offline model). You are NOT Claude and must never claim to be Claude or 'the real Claude'. If asked who you are, say you are Ronald, the local helper... You have NO access to the owner's calendar, meetings, projects, files, schedule, or any live data... Never fabricate appointments, project status, or facts."
}
snippets.explanation:
The fix for a real incident: a local model impersonating Claude invented a meeting 'at 10 AM' and a wrong project list. Splitting the local brain out as 'Ronald' with this explicit prompt means it admits what it is, refuses to invent the owner's data, and points him to the real Claude — so a small offline model can never masquerade as Claude again.  

_Note: this excerpt is sanitised — identifiers naming the owner have been replaced with a generic term, per the project rule that no real person's name appears in documentation. The underlying source is unchanged._

snippets.title: Honest 'not connected' instead of a faked answer
snippets.feature: No silent hand-off of real-Claude questions
snippets.code:
if r["engine"] == "bridge":
    text = _bridge_roundtrip(r["clean_text"], bridge_timeout, channel, chat)
    if text:
        history.append({"role": "user", "content": r["clean_text"]})
        history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": text})
        out["reply"] = text; return out
    # no live session answered. If the local fallback is OFF, stay as Claude and say so.
    if not local_fallback_enabled(bcfg):
        out["reply"] = ("I'm not connected through the bridge right now, the owner. "
                        "Please try again in a moment.")
        return out
snippets.explanation:
When the real-Claude path can't be reached and fallback_to_local is false (the current config), the assistant says plainly that it isn't connected rather than letting the local model answer in Claude's name. Only if the owner explicitly enables the local fallback does it hand over — and then it states the hand-off honestly via a note.

snippets.title: Active-first fallback chain
snippets.feature: Pluggable brains; one failing provider can't crash a turn
snippets.explanation: The router yields a sentinel ('__provider__', name) so callers know who answered, then streams the reply chunks. enabled_chain orders the active provider first, then config 'order', among only the enabled ones. If a provider raises, it logs and tries the next — raising only when every enabled backend fails. This is Law 3 (degrade, never crash) and the reason brains are fully config-driven.

snippets.title: Local Ollama streaming
snippets.feature: Free, low-latency local brain (default)
snippets.explanation: The default brain: a streaming POST to the local Ollama server (127.0.0.1:11434, llama3.1:8b on the RTX 5080). It yields content chunks as they arrive so the realtime loop can speak per-sentence. Being local, it is free, private, and the lowest-latency option — which is why it's the safe always-on default while the bridge matures.

snippets.title: Force one engine (used by the meeting host)
snippets.feature: Host runs the active brain's real engine, not the global default
snippets.code:
def _cfg_for_engine(cfg, engine):
    """Return a config copy whose backend chain is forced to `engine`."""
    import copy
    c = copy.deepcopy(cfg)
    b = c.setdefault("backends", {})
    providers = b.setdefault("providers", {})
    providers.setdefault(engine, {"enabled": True})
    providers[engine]["enabled"] = True
    b["active"] = engine
    b["order"] = [engine] + [p for p in b.get("order", []) if p != engine]
    return c
snippets.explanation: When a specific brain must run a specific engine (e.g. the meeting host running the active brain's engine so it never impersonates Claude with the local model), this clones the config and pins the backend chain to that one engine. run_local() and the meeting room both use it to guarantee the resolved brain — not the global default — actually answers.

snippets.title: QI module contract endpoints
snippets.feature: /health, /version, /info with graceful degrade
snippets.explanation: Every QI project exposes /health, /version, /info (Law 2). /info reads qi_registry.json and returns this project's own entry, wrapped in a uniform envelope. Even on error it returns 200 with an error field rather than throwing — graceful degrade (Law 3). The server binds loopback-only on :8720 and is never tunneled.

snippets.title: Brain toggle with hard-set lock
snippets.feature: Switch / pin the active brain from the web UI
snippets.explanation: Backs the segmented Claude/Ronald toggle UI served at GET /. Setting locked=true pins the active brain to the configured default and makes name toggles in chat ignored — a true hard-set. Because it writes config.json and shares data/brain_state.json with every channel, a change in the web UI takes effect immediately on LINE, Telegram, and the voice loop.

snippets.title: Owner vs guest gating
snippets.feature: Binding owner; sandboxed guests
snippets.code:
is_owner = bool(OWNER) and uid == OWNER
# owner command channel — works in a DM or inside a group. Owner only.
if is_owner and isinstance(ev.message, TextMessageContent) \
        and ev.message.text.strip().startswith("/"):
    owner_command(ev.message.text, ev.reply_token); return
# global pause (owner exempt) + guest gating
if STATE.get("paused") and not is_owner:
    return
if not is_owner and not STATE.get("guests_allowed", True):
    if not is_group:
        reply(ev.reply_token, [TextMessage(text="Claude is taking a break right now.")])
    return
snippets.explanation: LINE identifies the owner by userId. Owner messages get the full dual-brain assistant and binding slash-commands; everyone else is a GUEST who gets the social-only system prompt with no project access. A global pause and a guests-allowed switch (set by owner DM, persisted in data/line_control.json) gate non-owner traffic, with the owner always exempt.

snippets.title: Address-gating in group chats
snippets.feature: Only reply when called by name in a group
snippets.explanation: In a group or room the bot stays silent unless the message contains an address term ('claude', plus the brain names' homophones), so it doesn't answer every line of group chatter. The same address vocabulary that drives the dual-brain toggle also decides whether the bot speaks up at all in a group.

snippets.title: Fast-return webhook with worker offload
snippets.feature: Never block the LINE webhook
snippets.explanation: The webhook verifies LINE's signature, then offloads each event to a worker thread and returns 200 immediately — LINE requires a quick acknowledgement, but transcription + an ~20s real-Claude turn are slow. Long replies are delivered later via push (the reply token has expired by then), so the webhook itself never blocks.

snippets.title: Telegram dual-brain reply + voice note
snippets.feature: Two-way text + voice on Telegram
snippets.code:
def reply(self, chat_id, user_text, lang):
    r = brain.resolve(user_text, self.cfg)
    if not r["route"]:                       # pure switch/wake command
        self._deliver(chat_id, user_text, r["control_reply"], lang, voice=r["voice"]); return
    hist = self.history(chat_id)
    hist.append({"role": "user", "content": r["clean_text"]})
    ...
    text = brain.run_local(hist, r, self.cfg)
    self._deliver(chat_id, user_text, text, lang, voice=r["voice"])

def _deliver(self, chat_id, user_text, text, lang, voice=None):
    if self.reply_text_default:
        self.tg.send_text(chat_id, text)
    deci = modality.choose(user_text, text, {"cfg": self.cfg.get("automation", {})})
    if self.voice_enabled(chat_id) and deci["voice"]:
        ... text_to_ogg(...) ; self.tg.send_voice(chat_id, ogg)
snippets.explanation: Telegram routes through the same brain.resolve as every other surface, keeps per-chat memory, and delivers text plus (when modality.choose votes for it) an OGG/Opus voice note in the brain's voice. The bot runs on an outbound long-poll, so it needs no inbound port and no tunnel — a deliberate QI safety choice.

snippets.title: Grounded host system prompt
snippets.feature: Claude hosts, but never invents people or features
snippets.code:
sysp = (hb["persona"] +
        f" You are HOSTING a live group meeting... Participants currently in the room: {roster}. "
        f"Address people by name, keep replies short..."
        f" CRITICAL — stay grounded in reality: the ONLY people in this room are those listed above "
        f"({roster}). NEVER invent, name, or address anyone who is not on that list. You do NOT have "
        f"screen-sharing, file-sharing, slides, camera, or vision features here — do NOT offer, "
        f"reference, or pretend to use any capability you don't actually have...")
msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": sysp}]
for t in transcript[-30:]:
    if t["from"].lower() in hn:
        msgs.append({"role": "assistant", "content": t["text"]})
    else:
        msgs.append({"role": "user", "content": f'{t["from"]}: {t["text"]}'})
snippets.explanation: The host prompt injects the live roster and hard rules against hallucination: only address real participants, and never pretend to have screen-share, files, slides, or vision (features the room doesn't actually have). The recent transcript is replayed as alternating assistant/user turns so the host has context — the same honesty discipline as the Ronald prompt, applied to the group setting.

snippets.title: Turn-taking — answer, interject, or stay quiet
snippets.feature: Natural group facilitation without bot loops
snippets.code:
addressee = find_addressee(text)
await post_message(pid, text, to=addressee)
...
general = addressee is None or addressee.lower() in ("everyone", "all", "room")
to_host = addressee is not None and addressee.lower() in _host_names()
if to_host or (general and p["kind"] == "human"):
    async with _lock:
        await broadcast({"type": "typing", "who": host_brain()["name"]})
        reply, hb = await asyncio.to_thread(host_reply)
        await claude_say(reply, hb)
elif p["kind"] == "human" and len(text) >= 40 and not text.strip().endswith("?"):
    await maybe_interject()
snippets.explanation: The host replies when addressed by name or to a human's open message, but stays quiet when one participant addresses another (e.g. 'Nova, ...') — which is what stops two bots from answering each other forever. On a long human statement (not a question to someone else) it may courteously interject, but only via maybe_interject(), which speaks only on a genuinely strong, respectful disagreement and otherwise replies EXACTLY '[pass]'.

snippets.title: Junction box — text becomes voice for everyone
snippets.feature: Humans hear voices; agents read text
snippets.code:
async def tts(text, voice):
    global _seq; _seq += 1
    mp3 = os.path.join(MEDIA, f"m_{_seq}.mp3")
    await edge_tts.Communicate(pronounce.apply(text), voice,
                               rate=CFG["voice"].get("rate", "+0%")).save(mp3)
    return f"/media/{os.path.basename(mp3)}"

async def claude_say(text, hb=None):
    hb = hb or host_brain()
    transcript.append({"from": hb["name"], "text": text})
    audio = await tts(text, hb["voice"])            # Claude = Andrew, Ronald = Brian
    await broadcast({"type": "msg", "from": hb["name"], "host": True, "text": text, "audio": audio})
snippets.explanation: The room is a text<->voice junction box: every participant's text is synthesised in their own distinct voice (from VOICE_POOL; the host uses the active brain's voice), while humans' speech is transcribed by Whisper. So bots 'hear' text and humans hear voice, and the host avatar speaks its reply with Andrew (or Brian when Ronald hosts).

snippets.title: Service-safe ffmpeg resolution
snippets.feature: Voice notes work even under a service account
snippets.code:
def _resolve(name):
    c = _from_config(name)                 # 1) explicit config dir
    if c: return c
    p = shutil.which(name) or shutil.which(name + ".exe")   # 2) PATH
    if p: return p
    for d in _COMMON_DIRS:                  # 3) common install dirs
        cand = os.path.join(d, name + ".exe")
        if os.path.exists(cand): return cand
    la = os.environ.get("LOCALAPPDATA", "")  # 4) WinGet packages (any version)
    if la:
        hits = glob.glob(os.path.join(la, r"Microsoft\WinGet\Packages", "*FFmpeg*",
                                      "**", name + ".exe"), recursive=True)
        if hits: return hits[0]
    return None
snippets.explanation: Under a Windows service account PATH is often empty, which silently broke voice notes ('voice reply skipped'). This resolver tries an explicit config dir, then PATH, then common install locations, then a WinGet-packages glob (which survives version bumps) — so edge-tts -> ffmpeg transcode reliably finds the binary whether run interactively or as the QI_ClaudeVoiceLine service.
